generated_texts.prompt: [TOPIC] Business [\TOPIC] [ANS] In summary
generated_texts.raw_completion:
, the main purpose of this article is to discuss how a company can use its resources and capabilities in order for it achieve competitive advantage. The first part will be discussing about what are resource-based view (RBV) theory and dynamic capability approach.
The second section would explain why RBV has been criticized by some scholars as well as their responses towards those criticisms while at last we shall conclude our discussion with an overall evaluation on whether or not these two theories could help companies gain sustainable competitiveness over time through effective utilization management practices such as innovation strategies etc..
What Is Resource-Based View Theory?
Resource based views have become increasingly popular among business leaders who want more than just profits from investments made into new technologies like artificial intelligence software programs which require significant amounts of capital expenditure upfront but offer long term benefits when implemented correctly; however there’s still much debate surrounding exactly HOW one goes about implementing them effectively without running out money before seeing any return-on-investment whatsoever!
This type if investment requires careful planning so that you don’t end up wasting valuable funds trying something different every few months because “it didn’t work” – instead focus your efforts where they’ll yield maximum results! This means being strategic rather than reactive: knowing WHAT needs doing BEFORE attempting anything else AND having clear goals set beforehand otherwise things might get messy quickly…
Dynamic Capability Approach
In today's fast-paced world businesses need agility -they must constantly adapt themselves according to changing market conditions . To do this successfully firms should develop certain core competencies known collectively under Dynamic Capabilities Framework(DCF). These include:
1.) Sensing opportunities : A firm senses opportunity only after identifying potential threats posed against itself ;this helps identify areas requiring improvement within organization structure & processes .
2 ) Seizing Opportunities :- Once sensed ,a good manager takes necessary steps required seizing upon chance presented him/her i.e taking calculated risks leading toward desired outcome(s).
3 ). Transforming Resources:- Finally once seized chances transformed efficiently enough yielding positive outcomes then finally achieved goal becomes reality !
4.). Learning From Experience- Last step involves learning lessons learnt during entire process thus making sure next attempt succeeds better way possible !
